# 1 Kings Chapter 13 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** And-behold, a-man-of God came from-Judah by-the-word-of YHWH to Bethel, and-Jeroboam was-standing by the-altar to-burn-incense.

**2** And-he-called against the-altar by-the-word-of YHWH and-said, "Altar, altar! Thus says YHWH: 'Behold, a-son is-born to-the-house-of David — Josiah his-name — and-he-will-sacrifice upon-you ʾet-the-priests-of the-high-places who-burn-incense upon-you, and-bones-of men will-be-burned upon-you.'"

**3** And-he-gave on-that day a-sign, saying, "This is the-sign that YHWH has-spoken: Behold, the-altar will-be-torn, and-the-ashes that are upon-it will-be-poured-out."

**4** And-it-was when-the-king heard ʾet-the-word-of the-man-of God that he-called against the-altar in-Bethel, and-Jeroboam stretched-out ʾet-his-hand from-upon the-altar, saying, "Seize-him!" And-his-hand that he-stretched-out against-him dried-up, and-he-was-not able to-return-it to-himself.

**5** And-the-altar was-torn, and-the-ashes poured-out from the-altar, according-to-the-sign that the-man-of God gave by-the-word-of YHWH.

**6** And-the-king answered and-said to the-man-of God, "Plead, please, the-face-of YHWH your-God, and-pray for-me, and-let-my-hand return to-me." And-the-man-of God pleaded ʾet-the-face-of YHWH, and-the-hand-of the-king returned to-him and-was as-before.

**7** And-the-king spoke to the-man-of God, "Come with-me to-the-house and-refresh-yourself, and-I-will-give to-you a-gift."

**8** And-the-man-of God said to the-king, "If you-give to-me ʾet-half your-house, I-will-not come with-you, and-I-will-not eat bread and-I-will-not drink water in-this place.

**9** For so he-commanded-me by-the-word-of YHWH, saying, 'You-shall-not eat bread and-you-shall-not drink water, and-you-shall-not return by-the-way that you-came.'"

**10** And-he-went by-another way, and-did-not return by-the-way that he-came to-Bethel.

**11** And-a-certain old prophet was-dwelling in-Bethel, and-his-son came and-told-him ʾet-all the-deed that the-man-of God did that-day in-Bethel — ʾet-the-words that he-spoke to the-king — and-they-told-them to-their-father.

**12** And-their-father spoke to-them, "Which way did-he-go?" And-his-sons had-seen ʾet-the-way that the-man-of God who-came from-Judah went.

**13** And-he-said to-his-sons, "Saddle for-me the-donkey." And-they-saddled for-him the-donkey, and-he-rode upon-it.

**14** And-he-went after the-man-of God and-found-him sitting under a-terebinth. And-he-said to-him, "Are-you the-man-of God who-came from-Judah?" And-he-said, "I am."

**15** And-he-said to-him, "Come with-me to-the-house and-eat bread."

**16** And-he-said, "I-am-not able to-return with-you or-to-come with-you, and-I-will-not eat bread and-I-will-not drink water with-you in-this place.

**17** For a-word came to-me by-the-word-of YHWH: 'You-shall-not eat bread and-you-shall-not drink water there; you-shall-not return to-go by-the-way that you-came.'"

**18** And-he-said to-him, "I also am a-prophet like-you, and-an-angel spoke to-me by-the-word-of YHWH, saying, 'Bring-him-back with-you to your-house, and-let-him-eat bread and-drink water.'" He-lied to-him.

**19** And-he-returned with-him and-ate bread in-his-house and-drank water.

**20** And-it-was — they were-sitting at-the-table — and-the-word-of YHWH came to the-prophet who had-brought-him-back.

**21** And-he-called to the-man-of God who-came from-Judah, saying, "Thus says YHWH: 'Because you-rebelled-against the-mouth-of YHWH and-did-not keep the-commandment that YHWH your-God commanded-you,

**22** and-you-returned and-ate bread and-drank water in-the-place of-which he-said to-you, "Do-not eat bread and-do-not drink water" — your-corpse shall-not come to the-tomb-of your-fathers.'"

**23** And-it-was after his-eating bread and-after his-drinking, and-he-saddled for-him the-donkey — for-the-prophet whom he-had-brought-back.

**24** And-he-went, and-a-lion found-him on-the-way and-killed-him. And-his-corpse was-thrown on the-road, and-the-donkey was-standing beside-it, and-the-lion was-standing beside the-corpse.

**25** And-behold, men passing-by saw ʾet-the-corpse thrown on the-road and-the-lion standing beside the-corpse. And-they-came and-spoke in-the-city where the-old prophet dwelt.

**26** And-the-prophet who had-brought-him-back from-the-way heard, and-he-said, "It is the-man-of God who rebelled-against the-mouth-of YHWH. And-YHWH gave-him to the-lion, and-it-broke-him and-killed-him, according-to-the-word-of YHWH that he-spoke to-him."

**27** And-he-spoke to his-sons, saying, "Saddle for-me the-donkey." And-they-saddled.

**28** And-he-went and-found his-corpse thrown on the-road, and-the-donkey and-the-lion standing beside the-corpse. The-lion had-not eaten ʾet-the-corpse and-had-not broken the-donkey.

**29** And-the-prophet took-up ʾet-the-corpse-of the-man-of God and-laid-him on the-donkey and-brought-him-back. And-the-old prophet came to the-city, to-mourn and-to-bury-him.

**30** And-he-laid his-corpse in-his-own-tomb, and-they-mourned over-him, "Alas, my-brother!"

**31** And-it-was after his-burying-him, and-he-spoke to his-sons, saying, "When-I-die, bury-me in-the-tomb in-which the-man-of God is-buried. Beside his-bones lay ʾet-my-bones.

**32** For surely-coming will-come-to-pass the-word that he-called by-the-word-of YHWH against the-altar that is in-Bethel, and-against all the-houses-of the-high-places that are in-the-cities-of Samaria."

**33** After this thing Jeroboam did-not turn from his-evil way, but-he-returned and-made from-the-ends-of the-people priests-of high-places. Whoever desired, he-filled his-hand, and-he-became a-priest-of high-places.

**34** And-this thing became the-sin-of the-house-of Jeroboam, to-cut-off and-to-destroy from-upon the-face-of the-earth.

---
## EMET Textual Notes

1. **13:2 — "Josiah his-name"**: An extraordinary prophecy naming a king three centuries before his birth. This specificity is unparalleled in prophetic literature and will be fulfilled in 2 Kings 23:15-16.

2. **13:18 — "He-lied to-him"**: The narrator's blunt editorial: kichesh lo — "he lied to him." No ambiguity, no softening. A prophet lies to another prophet, and the one who believes the lie pays with his life.

3. **13:24 — the lion tableau**: The lion kills the man but does not eat the corpse or harm the donkey. This unnatural behavior signals divine purpose — the lion is an instrument of judgment, not a predator following instinct.

4. **13:33 — "did-not turn"**: Despite witnessing the altar torn apart and a miraculous sign, Jeroboam refuses to change course. This stubbornness becomes the template for every northern king who follows.

— EMET
